correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the overlap graph by shifting each word and appending ternary digits before forgetting direction, obtaining 38 distinct simple edges. Under technical labels 1 through 17 in the displayed order, all 38 edges agree with the union of cycle/shortcut edges in Petyuk v2, Appendix proof line 1, p. 7 (and 1=102 and 2=210 agree with p. 4). This cross-check uses the published proof text, not a direct visual reading of all Figure-2 word labels. Theorem 5 formally states non-word-representability of S(3,k); its Appendix proves the Figure-2 obstruction itself is non-word-representable. I checked the precise graph against that premise rather than independently re-proving the negative result. An independent replay (branches/independent_small_replays.py petyuk, with the frozen certificate.json as data) checked all 17 distinct omissions and verified each order was a permutation. Orienting all edges forward gives acyclicity. Across all deletions the replay visited 2391 nontrivial directed paths; none of length at least three edges had adjacent endpoints, so there is no shortcut. Paths of length one or two with adjacent endpoints already form a clique in a forward orientation. The semi-transitive characterization then gives word-representability of every deletion. For any proper induced subgraph first remove an omitted vertex and restrict the word or orientation. No inference to ambient minimum order is made.

evidence: Problem 1 asks if Figure 2 is minimum by number of vertices among induced obstructions in the 27-vertex S(3,3). The follow-up proves positive word-representability for structured S_m(n,k) families in the inspected passages, not arbitrary smaller subsets of S(3,3) or the 17 specific deletions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An actual affirmative ambient minimum-order theorem would dominate the frozen claim. The question is not such a theorem, and the inspected structured positive theorems do not place the requested deletion graphs in their scope.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Heredity only passes forward from a positive induced host to its induced subgraphs. Non-word-representability of a host is compatible with either sign for its deletions. The new positive orientations are the missing evidence for the precise deletion-criticality claim.

originality.rationale: The paper explicitly poses the stronger ambient vertex-count question but supplies the negative witness only for the full obstruction, not positive witnesses for the deletions. The closest accessible follow-up treats other structured subgraphs; the strongest catalogue match concerns S(4,3), not this obstruction. No equivalent or stronger established statement was identified in the inspected sources.
residual_risks: Bounded literature and catalogue comparisons cannot exclude unindexed solver checks or an independently obtained minimum-order result. No statement of priority or resolution of the ambient problem is made.

value.rationale: The object is the obstruction used to prove a published theorem, not an arbitrary slice. The exact positive deletion certificates settle a natural way of trying to shorten it and prove that any smaller ambient obstruction must use vertices outside this set. This is a useful partial advance on the expressly posed minimum-order question, without claiming to solve it.
